title: 79. Min Stack

examples.explanation: After pushing -2, 0, and -3, getMin returns -3. Pop removes -3, then top returns 0, and getMin returns -2.
After pushing 5 twice, getMin returns 5 and top returns 5. Pop removes one 5, then getMin returns 5.
After pushing 7, top returns 7 and getMin returns 7.

hints: Keep a normal stack and a second stack containing the minimum at each relevant depth.
Push to the minimum stack when a value is less than or equal to its current top so duplicate minima are handled correctly.
